A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InstanceGaussian. Their complete main texts, equations, algorithms, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original ScanNet and LeRF evaluations, representation and aggregation ablations, and qualitative GraspNet results.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, sensitivity and runtime experiments, sampling-variability results, and failure cases.

M1.justification: The shared-feature Gaussian representation, three training stages, truncated contrastive loss, FPS clustering, and graph aggregation remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithm 1. The ScanNet smoothing MLP was already documented in v1 Appendix A.3; the semantic-to-instance terminology clarification does not introduce a component.

E1.justification: Both versions use ScanNet, LeRF, and GraspNet for the same segmentation, querying, rendering, and qualitative generalization pipeline. v2 adds LeRF object renders and failure examples within this coverage, without establishing new datasets, task requirements, or altered input conditions.

E2.justification: The original comparators are retained, while Table 7 adds GAGA to instance segmentation and SAGA to instance and semantic segmentation. SAGA was previously only discussed as related work. Table 13 additionally compares aggregation against HDBSCAN, substantially extending the evaluated alternatives.

E3.justification: The original scenes, preprocessing, training schedule, and benchmark metrics are retained. Appendix C adds targeted protocols: mA50/mA25 reporting for existing ablations, FPS point-count sweeps from 200 to 1000, voxel-size and connectivity-threshold sweeps, and runtime measurements across point counts.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained representation/training and connectivity ablations, v2 adds hyperparameter sensitivity, random FPS initialization, aggregation runtime, and HDBSCAN substitution studies. Appendix E and Figures 12–13 add concrete analyses of incorrect SAM masks and unsuccessful aggregation of large, partially observed objects.

E5.justification: v1 contains no comparable variability reporting. v2 Tables 10–11 introduce ± summaries and explicitly report five different FPS starting-point samples. The meaning of ± is not defined, and these samples should not be interpreted as five complete training runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their numerical results, but Tables 6–13 add substantial comparative, accuracy, sensitivity, variability, and timing evidence. For example, HDBSCAN reports semantic/instance mIoU of 31.84/44.76 versus 40.66/50.27 for the proposed aggregation. Table 8 reveals that joint representation alone achieves higher mA25 than the full configuration, 84.42 versus 80.22. New renders and failure cases also extend the qualitative findings.

T1.justification: Appendix C.3 newly states an O(K²) complexity bound for merging. This is a limited mathematical addition; Equations 1–6 and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged, and no new proof or theorem is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding contribution statements retain the same three contributions and state-of-the-art segmentation claims. Terminology refinements and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit limitations concerning MLP-related computational cost, frequent SAM errors, and large-object fragmentation. Appendix E explains how incomplete object observations undermine feature consistency and aggregation. Appendix C also interprets robustness results and justifies prioritizing mIoU despite the newly disclosed accuracy tradeoffs.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 revises reported ScanNet training time from approximately 35 to 30 minutes and adds a timing comparison reporting 1847 seconds for InstanceGaussian. Appendix C adds merging-time measurements. Hardware, scene lists, preprocessing, densification settings, smoothing details, and the project-page disclosure remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for GAGA and HDBSCAN, associated with the new comparisons. The main related-work discussion and positioning remain substantially unchanged. Several other references receive publication or bibliographic updates rather than representing newly cited research.

P1.justification: Edits clarify semantic versus instance features, refine wording and headings, and add a funding acknowledgment. The conclusion gains a limitations paragraph, and the appendices gain dedicated comparison, ablation, and failure-analysis sections. The existing main narrative is largely retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is reorganized into scene rows and method columns and gains ground-truth panels. v2 adds structured experimental tables, a LeRF rendering montage, and two failure-case figures. Existing figures are relocated or resized; the GraspNet and feature-map figures are retained under new numbers.

improvement.justification: v1 left aggregation alternatives, parameter sensitivity, sampling stability, computational cost, and concrete failure boundaries largely untested or undocumented. v2 Tables 6–13 and Appendix E substantially address these gaps and expose accuracy tradeoffs obscured by the original mIoU-only ablations. This strengthens assessment of the unchanged headline results and makes the paper more transparent, although uncertainty summaries and some experimental details remain underspecified.
